Endocarditis Infective endocarditis caused by fungi such as Aspergillus or Candida is much less common than that caused by bac- teria (p.168). Mortality due to fungal endocarditis is high. Patients should be treated with antifungal therapy and in many cas- es surgical removal of an infected heart valve. Amphoter- icin B was most commonly used, usually alone but in some cases combined with flucytosine.1-4 Alternatives for endocarditis caused by Candida spp. are fluconazole or caspofungin. Voriconazole may now be the drug of choice for endocarditis caused by Aspergillus spp.4 Since relapse rates of up to 40% have been reported after stopping ther- apy, secondary prophylaxis is recommended with flucona- zole, itraconazole, posaconazole, or voriconazole (de- pending on the susceptibilities of the infecting organism) for a minimum of 2 years and in some cases for life.
